intro.title: Compound Component (Tabs)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a tabbed interface using React's compound component pattern. You will learn how to create a set of components (like Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanels, and TabPanel) that work together seamlessly while keeping their internal state and logic hidden. The core concept involves using React's Context API to share state and functionality between these related components without requiring explicit prop drilling. You'll use JSX for structure, React hooks for state management, and component composition for a clean, reusable design. By the end, you'll have a functional, customizable tabs component that demonstrates advanced React patterns in a beginner-friendly way.
intro.usecase: The compound component pattern is widely used in real-world React applications to build flexible and reusable UI sections. For example, product dashboards often use Tabs to switch between analytics, user management, and settings panels without reloading the page. E-commerce sites implement Tabs in product detail pages to separate descriptions, reviews, and shipping information, providing a clean user experience. Developers apply this pattern in admin interfaces, form wizards, and modal dialogs to create maintainable components that manage their own state and composition.
